✅ The ability to analyse performance data, prioritise work effectively and communicate insights in a way that non-technical audiences understand

title: Value Management & Financial Operations Lead
description:
Become a part of our caring community

At Humana , we are focused on maximizing the value of our investments and ensuring disciplined financial management across our portfolio of initiatives. In this role, you will lead financial operations, budget planning, forecasting, value management, and investment evaluation activities that support executive decision-making and strategic portfolio governance. You will partner across business, technology, finance, and operational teams to identify opportunities, quantify value, evaluate investment decisions, and monitor realization of expected outcomes.
The core work hours will be based on EASTERN time, with flexibility based on exact location.

The Delivery Lead oversees financial operations and value management activities that enable effective portfolio governance and investment decision-making. This role is responsible for operational budget management, forecasting, invoicing oversight, financial reporting, and performance tracking across a complex portfolio of initiatives.

The Delivery Lead develops business cases, identifies and quantifies expected value, supports investment evaluations, and establishes processes to monitor benefits realization. This role partners with leaders across the organization to evaluate new opportunities, assess strategic investments, and ensure alignment between financial commitments and expected business outcomes.

The selected candidate will establish portfolio-level reporting and scorecards, monitor expected versus realized value, identify risks and opportunities impacting financial performance, and provide recommendations to senior leadership to support strategic decision-making.

The Delivery Lead exercises independent judgment and decision-making on complex issues, works under minimal supervision, and requires strong analytical, financial, and stakeholder management capabilities.

Use your skills to make an impact

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead operational budget management, forecasting, invoicing, and financial planning activities.

• Develop and maintain portfolio-level financial reporting and performance scorecards.

• Partner with business and technology leaders to develop business cases and investment recommendations.

• Identify, quantify, and track expected value associated with strategic initiatives.

• Establish and maintain processes for value realization measurement and reporting.

• Support portfolio governance processes, including investment prioritization and funding reviews.

• Analyze financial and operational performance trends and make recommendations to improve outcomes.

• Communicate portfolio performance, investment recommendations, and realized value to senior leadership and key stakeholders.

• Maintain visibility into portfolio spend, forecast accuracy, and investment performance.

• Drive continuous improvement of value management and financial operations capabilities.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree or 7+ years of healthcare, finance, operations, strategy, or portfolio management experience.

• 5+ years of financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, or business operations experience.

• Experience developing business cases and evaluating investment opportunities.

• Experience analyzing and communicating financial and operational performance metrics.

• Experience leading highly complex cross-functional initiatives.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and executive communication skills.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and financial modeling.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting large-scale healthcare, technology, or transformation portfolios.

• Experience with benefits realization, value management, or portfolio management disciplines.

• Experience preparing materials and recommendations for executive leadership review.

• Knowledge of healthcare payer operations, Stars, Risk Adjustment, Clinical Data Exchange, or Technology portfolios.

Based in Washington, D.C., Quorum is the leading provider of workflow software and information services for government affairs professionals globally. We serve over 2,000 customers-including over 50% of the Fortune 100-across 30+ countries.
At Quorum , our "product" isn't just our software; it’s our people. We are looking for a 100% remote Senior Software Engineer to join our Engineering Team -the engine behind Quorum ’s AI strategy. This isn't just a coding role; it’s an opportunity to build the advanced AI solutions that help the world’s most influential organizations navigate the legislative landscape.
The Impact You’ll Have
As a Senior Engineer, you will own the end-to-end lifecycle of features that impact thousands of clients. You will bridge the gap between complex datasets and intuitive user experiences, leveraging AI to automate the "administrative drag" of public affairs. You’ll be a key architect of our unified codebase, ensuring our tools remain reliable, efficient, and cutting-edge.
Your Journey at Quorum

• First Week: You’ll hit the ground running and ship your first piece of code to production.

• First Month: You’ll be working across the stack-from infrastructure and APIs to the UI.

• First Six Months: You’ll take full ownership of a feature set, making technical decisions that directly impact our global client base.

• First Year: You’ll help guide the team on broad technical decisions that shape our stack and the growth of the entire company.

About You

• The Expert: You have 10+ years of experience building software for end-users, with deep mastery of backend languages (we use Python/Django) and relational databases (PostgreSQL).

• AI-Forward: You are excited about the potential of artificial intelligence and want to design systems that leverage AI to solve real-world problems.

• A Designer & Builder: You don't just write code; you design complex systems, write technical documentation, and implement your vision.

• The "Owner" Mentality: You care deeply about the quality of your code and are committed to building the skills of those around you through mentorship and thoughtful code reviews.

• Self-Starter: You’re a motivated professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is excited to pitch in wherever needed, from recruiting to customer support.

About the Software Development Team

title: Business Development & GTM Associate
description:
About Odyssey:

K-12 education is one of the most consequential determinants of a child’s future - and many families have had limited ability to shape how and where their child learns. Education Savings Account (ESA) programs along with the Education Freedom Tax Credit are changing that. One of the fastest-growing public education initiatives in the U.S., they give states the ability to put education funding directly in the hands of families, who can then choose the learning experiences that best fit their child - from schools and tutors to therapy, curriculum, and technology.

But once these policies are signed into law, states face an enormous operational challenge. They must stand up entirely new programs, manage the secure and compliant flow of public funds, approve and monitor thousands of vendors, support families at scale, and prevent fraud - all while delivering a high-quality user experience.

That’s where Odyssey comes in.

We partner with state agencies to design, launch, and operate ESA and school choice programs on their behalf. We provide the technology, program operations, vendor ecosystem, and family experience that make these programs actually work in the real world. Today, we operate across 10 states, and our platform powers programs serving 250,000+ students and over $2B in annual education funding - and we’re just getting started.

Most recently, we launched the Texas Education Savings Account (EFA) program - the biggest day-one ESA launch in the country - which has already received nearly 200,000 applications. It’s the kind of moment that captures exactly what we’re building toward: programs that work at scale, from day one, when it matters most.

We’re backed by respected investors, including a16z and Tusk Venture Partners, and we’re building the team that will take us to the next stage.

Odyssey sits at the intersection of GovTech, EdTech, and FinTech. We are a public-sector operator, a technology company, and a program delivery partner all at once. The work we do is civic infrastructure - it determines whether families can access life-changing educational opportunities.

WHY THIS WORK IS DIFFERENT

We’re in the weeds with state partners, internally with our product teams, and turning ambiguous policy into real systems that families depend on. This means building a platform that meets each state’s configuration needs while being flexible enough to support all customers. We are not building be-spoke software!

If you want a highly structured environment, this will feel uncomfortable. If you want ownership, speed, and problems that actually matter, you’ll feel right at home.

The Role

Odyssey is looking for an exceptional individual to help drive the company's next phase of growth, reporting directly to our Chief Commercial Officer.

This role is ideal for someone with a background in technology, startups, management consulting or another rigorous, fast-paced environment who wants to move from advising organizations to helping build one.

You'll work directly with Odyssey's commercial leadership across the full go-to-market lifecycle-from researching new markets and building pipelines to developing presentations, managing our CRM, supporting proposals and procurements, and helping advance major opportunities.

This is a high-ownership role. The work will range from highly strategic to highly tactical. We're looking for someone who is just as willing to roll up their sleeves and execute as they are to think strategically.

This is also not a traditional sales development role. You won't spend your day working from a call script. Instead, you'll have broad exposure to how Odyssey identifies markets, develops relationships, competes for business, and ultimately wins and launches major government programs.

title: MRB Mechanical Engineering Manager, Fury

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Dominance and Strike MRB Mechanical Engineering Team supports the production, sustainment, and airworthiness of Group 5 air vehicles and missile platforms. The team is focused on keeping fielded and in-production systems flying - evaluating nonconforming hardware, driving Material Review Board (MRB) dispositions, resolving production issues, and ensuring mechanical subsystems meet performance and safety requirements throughout their operational lifecycle. The team works at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing, and quality to maintain the pace of production without compromising airworthiness.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Lead and grow a team of mechanical sustainment engineers responsible for evaluating nonconforming mechanical hardware and determining engineering dispositions on fielded and in-production Group 5 air vehicles

• Hire, mentor, and develop engineers on the team, including establishing a path to MRB signature/delegated authority for team members

• Set technical standards and review complex or high-risk dispositions and repairs, acting as an escalation point for the most difficult nonconformances on mechanical subsystems, actuation, and structural-mechanical interfaces

• Own team workload and prioritization, ensuring dispositions and repairs are generated accurately and on schedule to keep production flowing

• Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, Design Engineering, and Supply Chain leadership to resolve cross-functional blockers and align on priorities

title: Contract Engineer, Automotive
description:
logcat.ai is the AI engineering layer for the operating-system stack. We build agentic systems for Linux and Android devices: we ingest the diagnostic artifacts a device emits (bugreports, logcat, dmesg, modem traces, ramdumps, perfetto, pcap, CAN) and help device makers diagnose, remediate, test, and author features across their OS stack, grounded in their own BSP. Think Datadog and Cursor combined for the OS layer. A VC-backed startup with a small, senior team - you work directly with the founders.

We recently raised a $2.55M pre-seed. The product is scaling and the customer list is growing. The team is still small, so you'll own what you build.

Build the automotive substrate adapter. Modern cockpit dumps are dual-OS on one SoC, and nobody diagnoses across that boundary well. You'll change that.

This is a scoped, deliverable-based contract with a path to a full-time Member of Technical Staff role.

A note on location

Remote, with at least four hours of overlap with Pacific or IST. We don't track hours. We ask for the overlap because a lot of this work is debugging together in real time, and that doesn't work across a twelve-hour gap. If you're in Seattle or Bengaluru, we'd like to meet in person now and then. It isn't a requirement.

The bar

• 10+ years of relevant engineering experience.

• Automotive embedded experience.

• AUTOSAR (Classic and/or Adaptive).

• CAN / CAN-FD and DBC-level fluency.

• UDS / DoIP diagnostics, SOME/IP, and ECU or domain/zonal architecture.

• DLT, with QNX a strong plus.

• Proficient in day-to-day work with CLI-based AI coding tools like Claude Code (or an equivalent). It's how the team operates, not a nice-to-have.

What you'll do

• Parse and correlate dual-OS cockpit dumps: QNX SLOG2, DLT traces, Android IVI logs, perfetto, pcap, CAN.

• Solve cross-clock-domain correlation across DLT ECU time, QNX monotonic, kernel monotonic, and Android boottime/realtime.

• Build the automotive diagnostic path: UDS, DoIP, DTCs.

Bonus

• AAOS or AAOS SDV, including VHAL.

• Hypervisor-based cockpits (QNX Hypervisor).

• Functional safety (ISO 26262) literacy.

• Vector toolchain (CANoe, CANalyzer).

What we offer you

• A front seat as we scale. Customer calls, the roadmap, the pipeline, how the company is actually doing.

• The AI tools you need. We use AI across writing code, reviewing it, research, ops, and internal tooling. If something would help you work better, we'll get it.

• Early ownership, and full visibility. We move fast, and you'll help decide where.

• A small team that's easy to work with. People here like solving hard problems and helping each other out.

What to expect after you apply

• Screening call with Head of People & Business Operations

• Technical conversation with Co-founder/ Head of Engineering

• Technical exercise with Co-founder/ Head of Engineering

• Final conversation with CEO

• References, then offer

In your application, tell us what you'd own here, and the hardest thing you've shipped in this domain.

- Hands-on experience building cash flow models and forecasts, and working directly with banking partners.

- Advanced Excel capabilities and experience tracking and reporting spend at a project or initiative level.

- Experience managing and developing people and resources within an operational finance team, with excellent communication skills and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.

- Industry experience within a high-growth tech or SaaS company.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today - and we’re just getting started.

ROLE OVERVIEW

We’re looking for an innovative and hands-on Senior Customer Marketing Manager to put Harvey’s EMEA customers centre stage: telling their stories, celebrating their wins, and building community around them.

Harvey has an incredible base of law firm and in-house customers across the region, and they are truly innovating the practice of law. Your first job is to elevate their voices: finding the customers doing standout work, earning their trust, and producing the written, video and spoken stories that put that work in front of the industry.

From there, the role expands into community programming: building the communities, programmes and moments (power user groups, customer roundtables, awards and recognition moments, customer-led content) that bring customers and the wider legal community together.

You’ll sit within the EMEA Marketing team and work hand in glove with our global Customer Engagement team, who own the overarching customer marketing strategy, programmes and playbooks. You’ll also partner closely with Customer Success and Sales. As the first dedicated customer marketer in the region, you won’t inherit a finished playbook. You’ll help write it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Localise the global motion for EMEA: take the programmes, playbooks and frameworks our Customer Engagement team builds globally and tailor them specifically for EMEA markets, customers and culture, working hand-in-hand to build a truly exceptional motion.

- Build the EMEA customer story pipeline: work across customer-facing teams to find the customers doing standout work, secure their participation and approvals, and keep a steady flow of stories in production.

- Tell their stories: own written stories, video stories, quotes and references end to end and to a standard the customer is proud to share.

- Get the stories seen: package each story for the channels that give it reach, localised for priority EMEA markets, and make sure Sales knows what exists and how to use it.

- Build the advocate bench: develop a roster of EMEA customers who can act as references, speakers, panellists and peer connectors, and track their participation so no one is over-asked and everyone gets recognised.

- Build EMEA community programmes: design and run the formats that bring customers together, such as power user groups, customer roundtables, practitioner communities, awards and recognition moments, each with clear goals and structured follow-up.

- Build repeatable playbooks and processes: the story production workflow, approvals process, reference tracking and community op

•
2 años de experiencia desarrollando en Java 11+ .

¿Qué competencias buscamos en el/la Software Engineer - Back-End Developer?

• Prote

• Contribute to technical sales documentation, reference architectures, competitive materials, and internal enablement resources.

• Maintain current knowledge of Virtuozzo products, the competitive landscape, and relevant cloud infrastructure technologies.

What You Bring

• Strong experience in sales engineering, pre-sales consulting, solution architecture, or a comparable customer-facing technical role.

• Experience supporting complex B2B software or infrastructure sales cycles.

• Solid knowledge of virtualisation, cloud infrastructure, storage, networking, Linux, or related infrastructure technologies.

• A strong understanding of modern infrastructure architectures, deployment models, configuration, integration, and performance considerations.

• Experience leading technical discovery, solution design, demonstrations, workshops, trials, or proof-of-concept projects.

title: Cloud Architect
description:
How we work ?

Ofelia Perks & Benefits
About the role
We are building our cloud offering to a full SaaS model, and building a new Architecture team to lead that shift.
You'll partner closely with our Head of Architecture on the software-and-cloud vision, and work day to day with the Cloud/DevOps and Platform teams. You'll have real ownership over how we build, secure, and scale the platform as it grows from where it is today toward a multi-tenant, multi-customer product.
How we work -Architecture built together
This role comes with real autonomy, on purpose. Our Head of Architecture will be closely involved at the start, introducing you to the teams and setting direction, and will then step back to let you drive your own scope. We're not looking for someone to manage closely; we're looking for someone who can take a blank page and own it, and who knows when to loop others in.
The Architecture team itself is still taking shape, so a lot of how we work will be built together with you. In practice, that means direct, frequent exchanges with the teams below rather than layers of process, closer to mentorship and architecture review than top-down direction:

• Head of Architecture (hiring manager) : software & AI architecture, partnering for a unified product vision

• Cloud/DevOps team : daily collaboration and mentoring

• Platform team : cross-cutting architecture topics

• Information Security Officer : validating cloud security choices

The day-to-day job
Day to day, you'll own the cloud side of that transition end to end:

• Design and evolve the platform's multi-tenant cloud architecture (tenant isolation, data models, onboarding flows), robust, scalable, and secure, with AWS as the primary provider and a second cloud provider

• Define and promote architecture best practices: high availability, resilience, cost optimization (FinOps)

• Lead containerization and orchestration with Kubernetes (cluster design, networking, security, observability, lifecycle management)

• Industrialize provisioning and deployments through Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and CI/CD pipelines (GitOps)

• Integrate and operationalize generative AI services, notably Amazon Bedrock (model selection, RAG, AI usage governance)

• Own the cloud security architecture, in partnership with our Information Security Officer, who covers ISO 27001/SOC 2 compliance: IAM, encryption, network segmentation, cluster hardening, threat modeling

• Define operational resilience practices: disaster recovery (RTO/RPO), backup strategy, SLA/SLO

• Mentor and upskill the DevOps and engineering teams

• Maintain active technology watch and challenge existing architecture choices

What success looks like
30 days: Understand and diagnose

• You've completed a full audit of the current platform: Kubernetes setup (shared cluster, namespace-per-tenant), network, IaC and CI/CD maturity, and you've mapped the gaps against a production-grade SaaS (HA, horizontal scalability, WAF, observability).

• You've built working relationships with the Cloud/DevOps and Platform teams and established a lightweight architecture review ritual with them.

• You share a prioritized diagnosis with the Head of Architecture: what's solid, what's at risk, what blocks our first customer.

60 days : Define the target and unblock

• The target multi-tenant architecture is documented and validated: tenant isolation model, HA strategy, horizontal scaling approach, and the security baseline (including WAF).

• The IaC and GitOps roadmap is defined, and the first components are managed through Terraform and automated pipelines.

• You've identified the integration pattern for generative AI services (Amazon Bedrock) and validated it with the Platform team.

90 days : Execute toward our first customer

• The critical gaps for production readiness (HA, scalability, WAF) are either resolved or scheduled with clear owners and dates.

title: Senior Electro-Mechanical Manufacturing Engineer
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Senior Manufacturing Engineer to join our team. The EW Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for Electromagnetic Warfare. This responsibility includes everything in the manufacturing value-chain, including, but not limited to, Design for Manufacturability work, tool design & selection, process creation & optimization, vendor sourcing & interaction, quality planning, and work documentation associated with the hardware that the Manufacturing Engineer owns.

As a Senior Manufacturing Engineer within EW, you will be responsible for driving process improvements, ensuring the highest quality of production, and supporting the development and implementation of new products. You will play a crucial role in optimizing manufacturing processes, reducing costs, and increasing efficiencies on existing technologies while also developing new products and scaling to full scale production.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own a portion or all of the manufacturing value chain that includes Assembly, Integration & Test (AI&T) for electro-mechanical assemblies

• Contribute to operational excellence with a strong continuous improvement mindset and leading impactful Kaizen events

• Be a strong partner with Product Quality Engineering to drive and support RCCA burndowns that tackle key issues both internally and externally to EW Production

• Collaborate with Design Engineering teams in early to late phases of the development process to provide DFx for smooth NPI transitions

• Develop process flows, breaking down large, complex assemblies into a logical part flow of subassemblies and sub-processes

• Write documentation required for successfully manufacturing their hardware at scale, such as work instructions, quality plans, inspection requirements, etc.

• Work with contract manufacturers across various disciplines (PCBA fab, metallic manufacturing, assembly, etc.) to develop repeatable, sustained processes for quick-turn development as well as at-scale production

• Work with technicians and other engineers hands-on, building prototype hardware

• Contribute to end-customer hardware mechanical or electrical design, including interconnects, board fabrication and inspection, etc.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Degree in a technical field preferred such as engineering, math, or a hard science

• 8+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing or design of electromechanical hardware

• Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment

• Demonstrated ability to contribute to the delivery of electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment

• Personal experience physically manufacturing hardware via any means (machining, fabrication, soldering, assembly, etc.) Work on personal or extracurricular projects is a plus.

• Prior experience working with JIRA, Siemens NX, Teamcenter (PLM), or Oracle (ERP) or equivalents

• Experience with RF Products that require system AI&T (assembly, integration, and test)

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

The Opportunity
Praxis is seeking an experienced Program Executive to lead one of our high-priority development programs in earlier-stage clinical development. This leader will own the cross-functional strategy, execution, and governance required to advance a potentially best- or first-in-class therapy through proof-of-concept and key value-inflection milestones, while building a clear path toward later-stage development.
Working across Research, Development, Regulatory, Technical Operations, Translational Sciences, Medical, and other functions, you will align teams around the most important questions, translate emerging data into decisive action, and drive high-quality execution. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, challenges assumptions, and knows when to accelerate, adapt, or stop.
Primary Responsibilities

• Lead the integrated program strategy and development plan through early clinical development, proof-of-concept, and preparation for later-stage development.

• Drive cross-functional execution, governance, and decision-making against program objectives, timelines, and key scientific, clinical, and business milestones.

• Partner across Clinical Development, Research, Translational Sciences, Regulatory, Technical Operations, Medical, Biometrics, Finance, and other functions to build an integrated evidence-generation strategy.

• Evaluate emerging clinical, translational, regulatory, competitive, and operational data to identify risks, opportunities, and alternative development paths.

• Lead preparation for key health authority interactions and ensure alignment across clinical, regulatory, CMC, and evidence-generation strategies.

• Represent the program with executive leadership, governance committees, partners, and external stakeholders while fostering accountability, transparency, and high performance.

• Proven cross-functional leadership with accountability for integrated program strategy and execution in Phase 1 and/or Phase 2 development.

• Direct ownership of program strategy, budgets, resource planning, governance, and investment recommendations for complex development programs.

• Experience integrating clinical, translational, biomarker, preclinical, regulatory, and competitive evidence to make sound decisions with incomplete or evolving data.

• Experience leading or preparing significant interactions with FDA and/or other global health authorities.

• Demonstrated ability to lead matrixed teams, resolve competing perspectives, and influence senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.

• Strong understanding of end-to-end drug development and the ability to connect near-term decisions to long-term product and patient impact.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience developing therapies in CNS

• Alliance or partnership management experience.

• Success operating in lean, fast-paced biotechnology organizations where leaders move fluidly between strategy and execution.

title: TMF Lead I
description:
Job Summary and Purpose:
TMF Lead is responsible for supporting project teams in maintaining a high quality TMF in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), other guidance documents, and Precision Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Senior TMF Lead takes on responsibility for the complex or challenging studies requiring an experienced TMF Lead. Additionally, the Senior TMF Lead supports and mentors more inexperienced TMF Leads.
Main Duties & Responsibilities:

• Ensure that TMF document review and processing, periodic quality review, set up, maintenance, finalization and archival of study TMFs is completed in a timely manner and with a high quality.

• Create and execute the study TMF Plan and project TMF Document Index. Ensure entire study team understands expectations, project-specific aspects of the TMF, and manage communication of any changes in the TMF Plan or Index to the project team.

• Ensure that TMF documentation (e.g. TMF Plan, TMF Index, Periodic Quality Review documentation) is filed in the TMF.

• Attend and contribute to project kick-off meetings, project internal or external meetings, and ad hoc meetings as needed to ensure the project team is aware of the status of the TMF, potential gaps and escalations.

• Engage and collaborate with the Project Manager and Functional Leads to ensure TMF documentation is submitted in a timely manner and with high quality in order to maintain the TMF in an inspection-ready state.

• Proactively anticipate challenges to TMF compliance and identify early signals of risk. Develop and implement plans to increase compliance and follows-up on non compliance. Follows TMF escalation process as needed.

• Ensure that TMF Risks are identified and appropriately documented and mitigated.

• Monitor and report on TMF Health and Metrics and escalate non-compliances and potential issues to internal team and Senior Leadership as required. Identify trends, risks, and overall status of the TMF and suggest mitigation strategies.

• Serve as point of contact and Subject Matter Expert (SME) for project audits or inspections and support in the report responses. Participate in Audit/Inspection interview. Escalate to TMF management in cases of significant risk to Precision.

• Ensure provision of TMF analytics and expertise to Sponsors.

• Ensure that Periodic Quality Review for assigned projects is initiated and performed by the Quality Review Specialists and ensure proper documentation.

• Ensure that document review and processing for assigned projects is performed by the Document Specialists on a timely and consistent basis.

• Identify project team TMF training needs and provide or support team re-education.

• Manage the close-out activities of assigned studies, including defining the timeline for final document submission, final document processing, close out of all outstanding queries, requesting the eTMF export from the vendor, transfer to the sponsor and collect the Acknowledgement of Receipt.

• Manage projects within the Sponsor eTMF System and actively listen to deliver insightful solutions for challenges.

• Monitor and report potential out of scope activities related to Records Management, communicate these to the TMF manager and Project Manager, and ensure out of scope tasks are properly added to change orders, if needed.

• Support and mentor less experienced TMF Leads on the performance of their role and problem-solving study-specific issues.

Bachelor’s degree (or its international equivalent) +5 years of related experience or equivalent combination of education, professional training and experience that provides the individual with the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job.
Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies:

• Working knowledge of FDA & ICH/GCP regulations and guidelines

• Demonstrates solid interpersonal skills

• Ability to identify issues and escalate appropriately and effectively

title: GTM Engineer (Fresh grad, India)
description:
Location: 100% Remote from India, min. 4h overlap with CET (e.g. 9:00-13:00 CET). Fluent English, spoken and written. German is not required.

Compensation: 20k-32k USD per year (depending on location) + Shares + Generous Benefits. We pay local rates that are at or above the market. We share this philosophy with GitLab https://about.gitlab.com/blog/2019/02/28/why-we-pay-local-rates/.

About Secfix

Secfix automates security compliance for SMBs and mid-market companies in Europe and gets them compliant with ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX and SOC 2 in weeks instead of months. We’re a fast-growing team of 36 people, backed by a $12M Series A from Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank) and Bayern Capital.

About the Role

You’ll be our first GTM Engineer and build the system our entire go-to-market team runs on, from BDRs to AEs. Today, everyone runs their own setup for data, outreach and communication. You’ll replace that with one central, automated system and keep it reliable as we grow. This is a hands-on engineering role: you’ll write code (Python, SQL) every day, connect APIs and build data pipelines and AI workflows, not configure tools or run RevOps. You report to our Head of GTM, talk to everyone in GTM, spot the biggest bottlenecks and decide together what to build next. We own products and outcomes, not Jira tickets.

What You'll Do

- Data: Make our CRM the single source of truth for every target account. Model accounts, contacts and buying committees, and build automated pipelines that pull data from multiple sources, deduplicate, score and write it back.

- Pipeline generation: Build signal-based outbound, inbound scoring and routing, and alerts that tell the right rep which account to call today and why.

- Sales automation: Build AI tools and agents that take repetitive work off our AEs, from research to proposals to CRM updates.

- GTM infrastructure: Design our central data layer, integrate new tools via APIs and webhooks, and make sure everything runs reliably: scheduled jobs, error handling, monitoring and alerts when something breaks.

- Ownership end-to-end: Investigate problems, find the root cause, ship the fix and document it so nothing depends on one person.

Your success: reps spend less time on manual work and more time with customers, and more pipeline comes from systems that run reliably and are actually used.

About You

You’re an engineer who loves building things real people use every day, and are curious about the business. You build systems that run reliably at 10x volume, not one-off scripts.

- Recent graduate (0-2 years) in Computer Science or another engineering field with a strong academic record.

- 1+ years of experience through your first full-time job or internships in a startup environment.

- Solid Python and hands-on experience with APIs and webhooks.

- You know how to run code in production: version control (Git), scheduling, handling errors and rate limits, logging and debugging.

- You think in systems: you understand how components depend on each other and what breaks when you change one part.

- Smart, structured problem solver and fast learner: you pick up new tools and technologies on your own and bring complexity down.

- Hands-on experience with Claude (incl. Claude Code or the API). This is a must-have.

- You’ve built and shipped real things (an automation, scraper, data pipeline or internal tool) and can show them.

- Independent, proactive and comfortable communicating remotely, especially in writing.

Nice to have: SQL and data modeling, experience with a CRM, GTM tools like Clay, a data warehouse or a cloud platform.

You should not apply if:

- You need detailed tickets telling you what to build.

- You only want to write code and don’t care about business impact.

- You don’t want to test, monitor and maintain what you ship.

- You’d rather be led than lead your own projects.

- You don’t want to work closely with Sales and the people who use your tools.
